headline: Tanker Hit by Projectiles North of Qatar
deck: A tanker was struck by multiple projectiles 51 nautical miles north of Qatar, with casualties reported, west of this month's Hormuz cluster.
body: A tanker sailing off the north coast of Qatar was struck by multiple projectiles, with a number of casualties reported, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency announced. [E1][E9][E11] At about 19:00 UTC, the master reported the vessel was "struck by multiple projectiles" about 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal. [E15] The British agency put the incident 51 nautical miles off Qatar, north of Madinat ash Shamal. [E10][E2][E12]
UKMTO did not say how many people were killed or injured, adding that authorities were investigating, and it did not specify the origin of the ship. [E3][E16][E4][E13]
Qatar has not commented on the reported attack, which falls within its exclusive economic zone. [E5]
It was the first reported attack on a tanker in the western half of the Gulf in weeks, The Maritime Executive said. [E14]

On 13 September this paper treated a hull hit at Hormuz as a question of whether one incident had bent the strait's flow count; on 4 October it recorded Iraqi crude still moving beyond the strait on a VLCC.
Attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz this month numbered nine by Tuesday, UKMTO said, representing half of the September total in the waterway and the Gulf combined. [E8]

Before the United States-Israel war on Iran began on 28 February, the strait typically handled about 125 large commercial vessels a day, and shipments through it accounted for about 20% of global crude and liquefied natural gas supplies. [E6]
In retaliation for US-Israeli attacks, Iran effectively closed the strait, while Washington has maintained a blockade on Iranian ports. [E7]

**The desk's reading.** A completed Hormuz transit is no longer the all-clear. UKMTO's October tanker-attack count was a strait tally; this hull sat north of Madinat ash Shamal, inside Qatar's exclusive economic zone, in the western Gulf. The last status on the vessel is a master's report after the strike, with casualties and an investigation; no source in hand records a sinking. The competing reading is that one unnamed tanker, with no death count, no flag and no wreck report, is still a single investigated incident and leaves the strait as the only demonstrated firing line. That reading is strongest if this remains the only western-Gulf projectile report. It does not erase the position already on the record.

**The next test.** The next UKMTO circular or Qatari statement by 21:00 UTC settles it. If that notice identifies the hull as under way or at anchor and logs no further western-Gulf hits, the one-off reading stands. If it warns traffic north of Qatar, records a second projectile incident west of the strait, or says the tanker is disabled in Qatari waters, the remainder-water reading holds.
